messages:
Anya L: Quick question — SOC2 reviewer flagged our SIEM export access and retention. who currently has access to the raw security events in Splunk? thinking we should tighten before the audit.
Matt G: Which export are you talking about? raw collectors from VPC/elb/app logs or the filtered alerts we push from the alerts pipeline?
Anya L: Both, actually. We stream raw network/app audit events into Splunk via the prod collector. Splunk retention is 365d today; raw S3 bucket (collector dead-letter/backups) is 7d. Concern is scope of who can query raw indices.
Dina R: Auditors will need longer access windows (>=365) for historical sampling. For engineers/devs we should do shorter windows and JIT access, e.g., 90d by default. Also: document rationale for SOC2.
Kevin S: Technical note: S3 backups are encrypted with CMK arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:111122223333:key/siem-prod-key. Key policy currently permits role redwood-siem-role + the audit-readers group. We can add conditions to the key policy to require session tags/approved MFA.
Matt G: We should avoid granting wide Splunk admin rights. Proposal: two new roles — siem-reader (read-only limited indices), siem-incident (read + tail for oncall), siem-admin (config). Provision via infra repo PR + terraform.
Jess T: SRE/Oncall needs tail/read for recent events during incidents — please ensure incident role can access last 30d by default and request extension via Jira for older data. We also need PII masking on certain fields.
Anya L: Agree. Also want export-in-transit and at-rest assurances in the RFC. Can we require collector TLS mutual auth and rotate certs every 90d?
Kevin S: Collectors use TLS 1.2 with cert pinning. We can add cert rotation job in infra pipeline. For KMS, we can require aws:ViaAWSService and enforce kms:EncryptionContext that includes "export=siem" to reduce accidental decryption by other services.
Dina R: Retention policy suggestion: developers/dev teams => 90 days; incident triage role => 180 days (with approvals); auditors/legal => 365 days. Raw backups in S3 should not exceed 30 days unless an approved exception is filed.
Matt G: Implementation plan: 1) RFC with roles + retention table, 2) Terraform changes (Splunk role mappings + KMS policy), 3) JIT access flow (Okta -> AWS SSO assume-role with approval), 4) quarterly access review.
sec-bot: Automated runbook link: https://redwood-internal/runbooks/siem-access. Example KMS policy change:
```
aws kms put-key-policy --key-id siem-prod-key --policy file://siem-key-policy.json
```
Kevin S: One more thing — we need logging for who assumed the SIEM roles (CloudTrail + Splunk audit). Make sure assume-role sessions include a ticket ID in session tags for traceability.
Dina R: Can we get a timeline? auditor rollup is in 3 weeks. I recommend locking down new default (90/180/365) within 10 days and exceptions workflow in 14.
Anya L: I'll draft the RFC today and assign owners: @kevin for KMS/policy, @matt for terraform + role mappings, @jess for incident role scoping, @dina for compliance sign-off. Will open JIRA and link here. :thumbsup:
